# core/diag

`core/diag` — how vector reports a problem and which exit code it ends with.

Every command ends with one of three codes: 0 when the check passed, 1 when
vector refused the input (a counterexample, a stale contract, a missing
test), and 2 when the command could not run at all (bad usage, a file that
cannot be read, a solver that will not start).

Generated from [src/core/diag.ts](https://github.com/amritk/vector/blob/main/src/core/diag.ts).

## Declarations

<a id="exit_pass"></a>

### EXIT_PASS

The check ran and passed.

```ts
const EXIT_PASS: i32 = 0
```

<a id="exit_refused"></a>

### EXIT_REFUSED

The check ran and refused the input.

```ts
const EXIT_REFUSED: i32 = 1
```

<a id="exit_usage"></a>

### EXIT_USAGE

The command could not run: bad usage, or an I/O or tool failure.

```ts
const EXIT_USAGE: i32 = 2
```

### Diagnostic

One problem vector reports: where it is, what it is, and the exit code it implies.

```ts
class Diagnostic
```

#### new Diagnostic

Makes a diagnostic.

```ts
new Diagnostic(file: string, line: i32, message: string, code: i32): Diagnostic
```

<scalar-field name="file" type="string" required>

the file the problem is in, or "" for none

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="line" type="i32" required>

the 1-based line, or 0 for none

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="message" type="string" required>

the text shown to the user

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="code" type="i32" required>

the exit code it implies, `EXIT_REFUSED` or `EXIT_USAGE`

</scalar-field>

#### Diagnostic.code

`EXIT_REFUSED` or `EXIT_USAGE`.

```ts
code: i32
```

#### Diagnostic.file

The file (or other source) the problem is in; empty when there is none.


#### Diagnostic.line

The 1-based line, or 0 when the problem has no line.

```ts

```

#### Diagnostic.message


### usageError

Makes a usage or I/O diagnostic, which exits 2.

```ts
function usageError(message: string): Diagnostic
```

<scalar-field name="message" type="string" required>

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="Diagnostic">

</scalar-field>

### refusal


<scalar-field name="file" type="string" required>

<scalar-field name="line" type="i32" required>

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="message" type="string" required>

</scalar-field>

### formatDiagnostic

Formats a diagnostic as `vector: file:line: message`, dropping the parts it lacks.

```ts
function formatDiagnostic(d: Diagnostic): string
```

<scalar-field name="d" type="Diagnostic" required>

the diagnostic to format

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="string">

</scalar-field>

### report

Writes a diagnostic to standard error and answers its exit code, so a
command can end with `return report(d)`.

```ts
function report(d: Diagnostic): i32
```

<scalar-field name="d" type="Diagnostic" required>

the diagnostic to write

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="i32">

the diagnostic's exit code

</scalar-field>
